title: Breakfast Sliders
subtitle: Mini sandwiches with sausage, egg, and maple glaze baked on one tray.
description: Mini brioche buns with sausage, egg, and cheese — slider format for crews who want variety without cooking ten different things.

ingredients.name: large eggs
ingredients.notes: folded into thin sheets on the griddle

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Breakfast Sliders in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Use everything bagel seasoning as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Sausage. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 350°F. Line a rimmed sheet pan with parchment. Cook sausage patties until fully cooked and fold eggs into thin rectangles roughly the size of each roll. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Slice the roll block
steps.instruction: Without separating individual rolls, slice the connected block horizontally into tops and bottoms. Keep the shape intact so assembly stays fast.

steps.title: Layer the sliders
steps.instruction: Place bottom halves on the pan. Add sausage, egg, and cheese to each roll. Cap with tops and press gently so stacks stay level. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Glaze and bake
steps.instruction: Whisk melted butter, maple syrup, and Dijon. Brush generously over roll tops. Bake until cheese melts and tops turn golden and sticky.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Rest and pull apart
steps.instruction: Rest 5 minutes, then cut along roll seams with a sharp knife or bench scraper. Serve warm from the pan or transfer to a hotel pan for the line.

stationWorkflow: Cook all sausage and egg sheets before touching the rolls—cold protein slows the bake and steams the bread.
Brush glaze right before the oven; a second light brush at the 10-minute mark adds shine without sogginess.
Cut and serve from the sheet pan at the line so the crew pulls their own portion without a bottleneck.
cleanupNotes: Discard parchment with stuck glaze rather than scraping—it saves time on a busy morning cleanup.
Soak the griddle used for egg sheets immediately; folded egg residue hardens fast once cooled.
leftovers: Wrap sliders individually in foil and reheat at 325°F for 10 minutes; add a fresh glaze drizzle after warming.
Split leftover sliders and griddle cut-side down for a crisp second-day breakfast with extra maple on top.
